title: Gene Ramey's story of Lester on the Southern bus
summary: Ramey told Freeman how Lester, Buck Clayton and Bud Johnson were threatened on a Southern bus and Lester laughed 'Shoot your pistol, baby.'

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: When Lester and Bud Johnson and Buck Clayton and some people were down in the Deep South, they went out on a party and the band, the Basie band left without them, the bus left, so they were on their own, expecting to catch a bus or a train since they knew where the next date was to be.
Well, in the Deep South this white bus driver refused to let them on the bus and Bud Johnson pulled an

instrument, and put it in the man's face, and said, 'listen you so and so mother, you are going to take us on this bus.' The man said, 'All right, you can go and sit in the back,' because the man was terrified. So they sat in the back and Lester -- here they were, everybody was tense and frightened and Lester Young claps his hands together like a little seal and says, 'Shoot your pistol, baby, shoot your pistol.'
Ramey Rainey told me that story, and it is just like the man. He refused to be frightened and always had this wonderful sense of humor, yet very deep.
I don't know that I should take the liberty of telling these stories.
Whatever they want to do about it, I would hope that if they don't use the story, you know, they delete it completely.
They won't, they will be very glad. What we are getting is very precious, but perhaps I am a little guilty. I have got to get you back, we have gone a long time.
